**WIKI PERMISSIONS — OPTIONS REVIEWED, DEFAULTS RULED, GDPR OVERLAY (rides the wiki front, mock-gated):**

MODEL (composed from existing rails, no new machinery):
1. **Per-doc roles** viewer/commenter/editor via people picker (m11449) — the base.
2. **Folder inheritance** — docs inherit folder grants, per-doc override wins; the share dialog shows WHERE each grant comes from ("inherited from /Projects").
3. **Org-visibility toggle** per doc/folder; **EU-lean default = private-to-creator**, org can flip its default via a Data&Logging policy row.
4. **Link sharing** = 2486 tokens with expiry+revoke; org-only links by default, PUBLIC links an explicit org policy opt-in.
5. Role-bundle groups (seat_match role → grant bundles) = later phase, schema ready, not built now.

GDPR OVERLAY (the compliance teeth):
a. **ERASURE OPTION**: a subject-erasure request finds every doc mentioning the person (the 1479 entity index — this is what the entity toggle feeds) → surfaces them for REVIEW (redact vs erase, never silent) → executes with cascade: doc content, entity links, VECTORS (2495 purge path), share grants, takeout manifests. Post-erasure = named absence everywhere. An erasure that can't cascade is non-compliant by construction.
b. **ACCESS REVIEW**: shares enumerable per org (ruled) + per-person view "everything shared with X" + ONE-CLICK REVOKE-ALL (offboarding made real). Every grant/revoke a touch.
c. **DEFAULTS FOR EU ORGS**: PII scrub ON (2495), entity analysis OFF until the org turns it on (the 1479 toggle — minimization by default), link shares org-only, retention per Data&Logging rows.
d. Takeout includes the share manifest + erasure log (portability + accountability).

MAKE IT HAPPEN: this lands as spec content on 1479 (entity/erasure), 1510/1993 (share UI), 2511 (org defaults + takeout) — spec_author each with this message as input, blocking questions to Fable, Alex pins the share-dialog mock before UI build.

**DEPENDENCY RULING (Alex): the core chain is explicit and lives in the graph as depends_on edges.** TICKETS depend on DOCS (specs, wikified tickets, proof pages all land in BB Docs — BBT without a working doc store is half a tracker); the WIKI depends on the WORKER (integral per today's 1479 ruling — no treatment, no wiki); CORPUS depends on both (folder → worker treatment → embed). Register the edges: bbt —depends_on→ bbdocs; bbdocs-wiki —depends_on→ wiki-worker; corpus-module —depends_on→ {bbdocs, wiki-worker, vectorize}. Consequences the graph must answer: (1) possibility()/context_pack cite the dependency chain when a build touches any link of it; (2) the WATERFALL CASCADES — a dependency down shows its dependents degraded-by-dependency (named: "degraded: wiki-worker down"), never independently green; (3) deploy/teardown ordering respects the edges (never ship a dependent ahead of its substrate); (4) the backup law (2512) prioritizes by dependency depth — the stores most depended-upon back up first. This is the general rule, not just these three: every service registers its depends_on edges at landing, and an edge-less service with obvious dependencies is a lint finding.

**DEPENDENCY MODEL (Alex asked how) — same quad substrate, no new table:** a depends_on edge is one row in the existing edge shape: (s=dependent, p=depends_on, o=dependency) + ctx {criticality: hard|soft, since, declared_by}. DERIVED, not hand-typed, wherever possible: a worker's wrangler bindings (D1/R2/Vectorize/DO/service-bindings) READ from the CF API = its hard edges for free — the 191-worker backfill emits depends_on edges in the same derivation pass; fetch-consumed services declare at register() or get observed from usage. Three computed views over the edges: transitive closure → waterfall cascade ("degraded: X down"); topological sort of hard edges → deploy order; depth count → backup priority (2512). And CONFIRMED, the circle Alex named: **Payload config is built via template FROM the graph** — graph rows (field specs, policy rows, dependency edges) are the source, the payload-collection template stamps the config, the admin UI materializes over it. The graph describes; templates stamp; Payload renders. Nothing configured by hand twice — the graph is the single declaration point, and the dependency edges are just more rows the same templates can read.
